extracted.intended_audience: AI companies and their legal/compliance teams, consumer protection stakeholders, policymakers, and the interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and enforcement-focused criteria the Federal Trade Commission applies to AI-related products, services, and marketing (e.g., business-opportunity ads, chatbots, AI-detection tools, subscription billing). Includes reporting obligations, misrepresentation prohibitions, and typical remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deceptive marketing of business opportunities (earnings/growth/refund guarantees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies marketing business opportunities must not mislead entrepreneurs or small businesses with claims about business growth, earnings potential, or refund guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language from the page: 'Air AI and its Owners will be Banned from Marketing Business Opportunities... the Company Misled Many Entrepreneurs and Small Businesses' and the complaint alleges 'deceptive claims about business growth, earnings potential, and refund guarantees.' Remedy examples: settlement terms can ban the company from marketing such opportunities and require other relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unauthorized subscription charges or deceptive billing
rubrics_metrics.description: Firms must not charge consumers for subscriptions without authorization or use deceptive billing tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by NGL: 'charged for a subscription to the anonymous messaging app NGL without their authorization' and the FTC 'launched a refund claims process for some consumers who were charged... without their authorization.' Enforcement may include refund processes and other relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not unfairly market to children and teens
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising and promotion must not unfairly target or exploit children and teens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the NGL matter: the FTC alleged violations including 'unfairly marketing the service to children and teens.' Such targeting can be a distinct basis for enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-generated reviews/testimonials must not fabricate or deceive
rubrics_metrics.description: Services that generate consumer reviews or testimonials must not produce detailed false or fabricated content that would deceive consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the Rytr matter: the complaint alleges the service 'generated detailed reviews that contained specific, often material details that had no relation to the user’s input... almost certainly would be false' and the proposed order would 'bar the company from advertising, promoting, marketing, or selling any service dedicated to – or promoted as – generating consumer reviews or testimonials.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims about accuracy or efficacy of AI tools must be truthful and substantiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must not misrepresent the accuracy, efficacy, or capabilities of AI products (e.g., AI content detectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Workado was found to have 'misrepresented the accuracy of its Artificial Intelligence content detection product' and the FTC 'approved [a] final order... requiring the company to stop advertising the accuracy or efficacy of its artificial intelligence (AI) content...' Remedies can include prohibitions on advertising specific claims and additional relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not promote AI as an unauthorized licensed profession (e.g., 'AI Lawyer')
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must avoid deceptive claims that AI substitutes for licensed professionals or provides professional services it is not authorized to deliver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoNotPay matter: the FTC 'Finalizes Order with DoNotPay That Prohibits Deceptive 'AI Lawyer' Claims, Imposes Monetary Relief, and Requires Notice to Past Subscribers.' Enforcement can include prohibiting deceptive branding, imposing monetary relief, and requiring notice to affected users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business opportunity operators must not falsely guarantee earnings or misrepresent AI-driven profit assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators selling business-opportunity programs or 'done-for-you' storefronts must not guarantee or falsely represent that AI-powered tools will produce specific income or passive earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by FBA Machine/Passive Scaling, Ascend Ecom, and Ecommerce Empire Builders: complaints allege false guarantees of making 'thousands of dollars a month in passive income' using 'AI-powered software' and charging consumers tens of thousands of dollars. Remedies seen include court orders halting schemes, receivership, asset turnover, and bans on selling business opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory reporting (6(b) orders) for generative AI companion products: advertising, safety, data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The FTC may issue 6(b) orders requiring companies that offer generative AI companion products or services to file special reports about their advertising, safety, and data handling practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page materials: '6(b) Orders to File Special Report Regarding Advertising, Safety, and Data Handling Practices by Companies Offering Generative Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) Companion Products or Services' and related files (Model Order, Cover Letter). These are compulsory processes to collect information about company practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure, test, and monitor consumer-facing AI systems for potential harms and disclose practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Firms operating consumer-facing AI chatbots or companion systems must measure, test, and monitor the systems for potential risks and be prepared to disclose how they do so in response to FTC inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the FTC inquiry: the agency issued orders 'seeking information on how these firms measure, test, and monitor potentially...' (harms). The inquiry targeted seven companies and seeks documentation and descriptions of testing/monitoring and mitigation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement remedies commonly used by the FTC for AI-related misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The FTC uses a range of remedies against companies that violate consumer protection laws in AI contexts, including bans on certain marketing or sales, monetary relief, refund processes, asset turnover, notice to subscribers, receivership, and reopening prior consent orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page: permanent bans (e.g., 'permanent ban of e‑commerce business opportunity scheme operator'), refund claims processes (NGL), 'turn over assets to the Federal Trade Commission to be used for refunds to consumers', 'reopen and set aside' prior orders (Rytr), and monetary relief (DoNotPay). These illustrate the kinds of corrective and preventive relief the FTC seeks.
